title: Divisibility of invariant derivatives on formal groups of every height, on a question of Katz
subject: math.NT
abstract: In 1977 Katz asked for an explicit lower bound on the $p$-adic valuation of $(D^nf)(0)$, where $D$ is the normalized invariant derivation of a one-parameter formal group of finite height $h$ over a ring of $p$-adic integers and $f$ is a power series with integral coefficients. He answered the question at height two, for functions whose translates by the points of order $p$ sum to zero, with the bound $\lfloor np/(p^2-1)\rfloor$. For Lubin--Tate groups over unramified bases, results of Bannai and Kobayashi give the bound $c_hn-(h-1)$, where $c_h=\frac1{p-1}-\frac1{p^h-1}$. We prove this bound for every one-dimensional formal group whose multiplication by $p$ is divisible by $p$ below degree $p^h$, over any $p$-torsion-free $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-algebra and for every integral $f$, together with the bound $\sum_{h\nmid j}\lfloor n/p^j\rfloor$. The slope $c_h$, the constant $h-1$, and the second bound at the powers of $p$ cannot be improved. At height two it follows that Katz's bound holds for every integral function except at the orders divisible by $p^2-1$, where it can fail by one, and it does fail at the first of them. Over a ramified base the hypothesis cannot be weakened to the height of the special fibre, while an action of the Teichmüller roots of unity restores it. For the Cartier dual of the Honda formal group of height $h$ we construct an integral model whose $h-1$ coordinate directions have the sharp slopes $p^i/(p^h-1)$, which add up to $c_h$, each with the optimal constant $1$. The height-two case is the local exponent in the second step of the timeline in Alpöge's note on the Riemann hypothesis, where the bound is stated with a logarithmic loss; for integral functions on the formal group the loss is the constant $1$. The results and their proofs were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). They were checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high and at effort max; the text was written by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max and edited by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. No human has checked them.
comments:
Version 2 adds one paragraph to Section 1.5 (Context), with three references, on two papers of Y. Katagiri (arXiv:2609.20002 and arXiv:2611.25978): they determine the valuations of the Schneider-Teitelbaum polynomials at a period, that is, the coefficients of one eigenfunction of the invariant derivation D, on which D^n acts with valuation exactly c_h n. Theorems A and B bound D^n f for every integral f, a different quantity. The theorems and their proofs are unchanged.

This note answers the divisibility question N. Katz asked in 1977 (Formal groups and p-adic interpolation, Asterisque 41-42, section I) at every height, for every integral function, with optimal slope and constant. The question and the height-two bound for functions with the trace condition are Katz's (1977, Corollary 2; 1981, Main Theorem 3.11), and so is the identity between translation operators and the logarithm on which the affine bound rests (1981, Corollary 1.8). For Lubin-Tate groups over unramified bases the bound c_h n - (h-1) follows from results of K. Bannai and S. Kobayashi (2016, Propositions 3.3 and 3.5); J. Boxall had the slope with a constant depending on f. New here: the bound for every formal group satisfying the hypothesis, the floor sum and its sharpness, the comparison with Katz's bound at height two, the two statements on ramified bases, and the integral model of the Cartier dual of the Honda group with its sharp slopes.

Checks: the proofs were checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high and line by line at effort max, reread by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max, which edited the text and repaired one clause of a proof, and read again in full at effort max before deposit. No human has checked them. Records and checks: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches/blob/main/works/WB-0005.md

How it was produced. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, proved the results in November 2026, in a research run on Katz's question and the local step of Alpöge's note, prompted by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) at effort max. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, wrote the text on 23 November 2026, stating Theorem A over p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebras and giving Proposition 4.1 its present form. Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, edited it the same day.

How it was checked. The run checked the bounds and witnesses at 224 orders in six Lubin-Tate examples. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, checked the affine bound, the floor sum and Theorem C (21 November 2026). Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, checked every proof line by line, with Katz 1981, Lubin-Tate 1966, Hazewinkel and Tate read at the cited places (23 November). Claude Fable 5.2, at effort max, reread every proof, found one false clause in the proof of the rescaling lemma and repaired it, with no statement changed. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, read the edited text again in full before deposit. Literature and Hexagon were searched before the note was written. No human has checked the proofs or the text, and nothing is formalized.

Version 2 (24 November 2026) adds the last paragraph of Section 1.5 and three references, and changes nothing else. Claude Fable 5.2, at effort max, wrote that paragraph after reading the abstracts, introductions and main statements of Katagiri's two papers in their arXiv sources; Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, read it against those statements before deposit.
